name: push-banner help
description: Help mode entries for plugin:push-banner. Drafts (draft: true) were written from the code by framework/cli/help-coverage.mjs --draft; edit them into plain English and drop the draft flag.
author: AmberX AXF

entries.title: Pull main in
entries.text: Brings main's newer commits into this branch, so it can merge.

entries.title: Hand to Claude
entries.text: Gives this to headless Claude Code on the VPS to sort out.

entries.title: Hide (every device)
entries.text: Hides it from the banner on every device.

entries.title: Merge
entries.text: Merges this PR — only once it's up to date with main and CI is green.

entries.title: Repair on the VPS
entries.text: Fixes this checkout on the VPS (a veto call).

entries.title: Remove from Pull failed
entries.text: Takes it off the Pull failed list on every device.

entries.title: Repair all on the VPS
entries.text: Fixes every broken checkout on the VPS.

entries.title: Hand failed pulls to Claude
entries.text: Every pull that conflicts goes to headless Claude Code on the VPS by itself.

entries.title: Pull main into all
entries.text: Brings main into every branch that's behind.

entries.title: Pull main into the group
entries.text: Brings main's newer commits into every branch in this group.

entries.title: Hand failures to Mosses
entries.text: Failures go to Mosses (Claude Code on the VPS) by itself.

entries.title: Any shell command
entries.text: Lets the fixer run any shell command. Leave it off unless you trust it.

entries.title: Branches not on main
entries.text: Shows “Branches not on main”. Part of Build Breaker.

entries.title: Auto-land finished builds
entries.text: On for every build by default. A build lands the moment it finishes: its branch is pushed, main merged in (builds files newer wins, THREADS and logs kept from both sides), its PR opened and put in the merge queue. A code clash or red tests gets a P0 'merge main and land' fix build, retried until it lands, with an FYI to you each time. Running builds get main merged in every 30 minutes.

entries.title: Wait for UI Review
entries.text: On: a PR waits until you approve its screenshots in UI Review, then merges by itself. Off: UI Review never holds a merge.

entries.title: Land now
entries.text: Lands this build at the next round (within 3 minutes), ahead of the others. Releases a hold.

entries.title: Hold
entries.text: Keeps this finished build from landing until you release it.

entries.title: Release
entries.text: Lets a held build land again.

entries.title: Merge queue
entries.text: Opens the merge queue: every finished build lands through it. The ready PRs are combined into one batch build, CI runs once on it, and a green batch lands on main as one commit.

entries.title: Jump to front
entries.text: Puts this PR first in the merge queue. Only your own click can do this.

entries.title: Remove from queue
entries.text: Takes this PR out of the queue until its next commit. The ones behind it get retested without it.

entries.title: Add back
entries.text: Puts a kicked-out PR back in the queue as it is, to be tested again.

entries.title: Add to queue
entries.text: Puts a PR you took out back in the merge queue.

entries.title: Add to Home
entries.text: Shows the merge queue as a card on Home.

entries.title: Merge queue
entries.text: On: each PR is tested once on top of main and the PRs ahead of it, then merges with no second run.

entries.title: Batch: one build, one CI run
entries.text: On: the ready PRs are combined into one build, CI runs once on it, and a green batch lands on main as that one commit. A red batch is split in half until the PR that broke it is found and kicked out. Off: each PR is tested on its own.

entries.title: PRs in one batch
entries.text: How many ready PRs go into one batch build (1 to 20). More means fewer CI runs; a red batch costs a few extra runs to find the PR that broke it.

entries.title: Merge queue: everything lands through it
entries.text: Turns “Merge queue: everything lands through it” on or off. It takes effect straight away and is remembered. Part of Push banner.

entries.title: Batch: one build, one CI run
entries.text: Turns “Batch: one build, one CI run” on or off. It takes effect straight away and is remembered. Part of Push banner.

entries.title: PRs in one batch
entries.text: Where you set “PRs in one batch”. Change it and the app uses the new value. Part of Push banner.

entries.title: Auto-land (one build)
entries.text: This build's own switch. On (the default): it lands by itself the moment it finishes. Off: it waits for you; every other build still lands.

entries.title: Landing chip
entries.text: How many finished builds are not on main yet, and how many have been stuck for over 30 minutes. Click it to open the landing line.

entries.title: Landing line
entries.text: Opens the landing line: every finished build not on main yet in landing order, the ones stuck for over 30 minutes with why and their fix build, and the last sweep.

entries.title: Sweep now
entries.text: Runs the sweeper at the next round (within 3 minutes): every finished build not on main is landed or gets its P0 fix build. It also runs by itself every 10 minutes.

entries.title: One at a time: the landing line
entries.text: The serial lander (on by default). Every finished build joins the landing line the moment it is built and lands on its own: main merged into its branch, generated files regenerated, CI run once on that head (a cancelled run is started again, never counted as a failure), merged on green. Red: a P0 fix build with your words and the failing check, and the line moves on. Off: the older batch or per-PR stack. Also: axf land status, GET /land/lander, voice "what's landing".

steps.say: Every finished build lands by itself, one at a time: main is merged into its branch, generated files are regenerated, CI runs once on that head and it merges on green. A cancelled CI run is started again, never counted as a failure.
Red after the merge: a P0 fix build is filed with your words and the failing check, and the line moves straight on to the next build. A code clash is flagged the same way.
The drift keeper merges main into every running build every 30 minutes (never into a worktree mid-edit or held by its session), so nothing gets hundreds of commits behind.

Every build grid has a Landing column: how many commits the build is behind main and where its landing stands. A finished build left unlanded for over 15 minutes turns the systems check red and is put in the line by itself.
Everything here is also axf land status, backlog, one, archive, flag, fresh and dispatcher, the /land REST routes, MCP and voice.
